title: Integral descent of a subset represented by a quasi-compact flat monomorphism
statement: Let $Z$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $q:Y\to Z$ be an integral surjective morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $H\subseteq|Z|$ be any subset. Suppose that $j\prime:F\prime\to Y$ is a quasi-compact flat monomorphism with image $q^{-1}(H)$. Here flatness is stalkwise flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism], quasi-compactness means that inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and monomorphism means that $\operatorname{Hom}(T,F\prime)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y)$ is injective for every scheme $T$. Then there exists a quasi-compact flat monomorphism $j:F\to Z$ with image $H$, together with an isomorphism $F\prime\simeq Y\times_Z F$ over $Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular there is a morphism $p:F\prime\to F$ making the square with $j\prime,j,q$ cartesian. No finiteness of the fibres of $q$, no flatness of $q$, and no Noetherian hypothesis on $Y$ are required.

source.place: §3, Theorem 3.3 (heading OCR 3.4), printed pp.12–13, case (ii), together with §1 Proposition 1.2 and Corollary 1.3 for uniqueness and the cartesian identification. Primary scan: https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf . Local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Put $H'=q^{-1}(H)$. By [lem-sfb-qc-flat-monomorphism-ringed-image], $H'$ is generalization stable. If $z$ generalizes a point $h\in H$, choose $y\in Y$ over $z$. The closed subset $q(\overline{\{y\}})$ contains $z$, hence $h$, because $q$ is closed by [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed]. Thus some specialization $y_h$ of $y$ lies over $h$. Since $y_h\in H'$, generalization stability gives $y\in H'$ and $z\in H$. For any affine open $D\subset Z$, $q^{-1}(D)$ is affine by the definition of integral morphism, so $(j')^{-1}(q^{-1}D)$ is quasi-compact. Its continuous image under $qj'$ is $H\cap D$, which is therefore quasi-compact. This proves retrocompactness: a quasi-compact open is covered by finitely many affine opens, and its intersection with $H$ is their finite union.

source.place: Theorem 3.3, proof 1°, printed p.12; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Regard $F'$ canonically as $Y|_{H'}$ by [lem-sfb-qc-flat-monomorphism-ringed-image]. By [lem-sfb-qc-flat-monomorphism-affine-neighbourhood], choose an open $U'\subset Y$ containing $H'$ such that $F'\to U'$ is affine. The subset $K=q(Y\setminus U')$ is closed and disjoint from $H$: a point over $H$ belongs to $H'\subset U'$. Thus $W=Z\setminus K$ is an open neighbourhood of $H$ and $q^{-1}W\subset U'$. Fix any affine open $D\subset W$. Then $Y_D=q^{-1}D$ is affine since $q$ is integral, and $F'_D=(j')^{-1}(Y_D)$ is affine: the restriction $F'_D\to Y_D$ is the base change of the affine arrow $F'\to U'$, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] applies.

source.place: Theorem 3.3, proof 2°, printed p.12; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $E_D=D|_{H\cap D}$ with the actual inverse-image structure sheaf [def-a1-ringed-subspace]. Step 1 supplies both hypotheses of [lem-sfb-generalizing-subset-affine-envelope]. Write its affine envelope as $k:E_D\to V$ and $h:V\to D$, and put $B=h(|V|\setminus k(H\cap D))$. That node gives $h^{-1}(H\cap D)=k(H\cap D)$, hence $B\cap H=\varnothing$. We prove $B=\varnothing$. If it were nonempty, [lem-sfb-subset-maximal-generalization], applied to the Noetherian affine scheme $D$, would give $b\in B$ with no strict generalization in $B$. Here $D$ is Noetherian because $Z$ is locally Noetherian and $D$ is affine; no condition on $Y$ has been introduced.

source.place: Theorem 3.3, proof 2° and 4°, printed pp.12–13; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Make the canonical localization $c:T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{D,b}\to D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], its image consists precisely of the generalizations of $b$. By [lem-sfb-generalizing-subset-affine-envelope], the envelope of $E_T=T|_{c^{-1}(H)}$ is $V_T=V\times_DT$, and its boundary image is $c^{-1}(B)$. Maximality of $b$ makes this image just the closed point $b_T$ of $T$. Since $b\notin H$, this closed singleton is disjoint from $c^{-1}H$. Its closure is itself. The boundary criterion therefore shows that $E_T$ is a scheme, with a quasi-compact flat monomorphism $i_T:E_T\to T$. This is a scheme conclusion obtained only after applying the boundary criterion; it is not assumed while forming the envelope.

source.place: Theorem 3.3, proof 4°, first half, printed p.13; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Set $Y_T=Y_D\times_DT$ and $P=F'_D\times_DT$. The morphism $Y_T\to T$ is integral by [lem-sbc-integral-morphism-base-change] and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. In particular $Y_T$ is affine. The arrow $P\to Y_T$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and is a quasi-compact flat monomorphism by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]; monicity follows directly by cancelling the $F'_D$ components in the pullback universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its image is exactly the inverse image of $c^{-1}H$, since surjectivity of a base change gives a point above every point of the inverse-image subset. Thus $P$ is affine. The factorization characterization in [lem-sfb-qc-flat-monomorphism-ringed-image], applied to $P\to Y_T$ and $E_T\to T$, says for every test scheme $L$ that a map $L\to Y_T$ lifts to $P$ exactly when its composite to $T$ has image in $c^{-1}H$, exactly when it lifts to $E_T$. All lifts are unique, so the resulting square is cartesian by the fibre-product universal property.

source.place: Theorem 3.3, proof 4°, cartesian identification and affine source, printed p.13; factorization supplied by §1 Proposition 1.2; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Consequently $P\to E_T$ is the base change of $Y_T\to T$, hence integral and surjective by [lem-sbc-integral-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The integral case of [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-affine-target] applies because $P$ is affine, and proves that $E_T$ is affine. The final equivalence in [lem-sfb-generalizing-subset-affine-envelope] now makes $k_T:E_T\to V_T$ an isomorphism. Its complement is empty, contradicting the boundary image $\{b_T\}$ obtained in Step 4. Therefore the original $B$ is empty. The same envelope equivalence shows that $E_D\simeq V$ is an affine scheme, whose canonical arrow $E_D\to D$ is a quasi-compact flat monomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 3.3, proof 4°, second half, printed p.13; its Proposition 3.1(ii) is supplied by the stronger existing Stacks 05YU node; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The induced ringed space $F=Z|_H$ [def-a1-ringed-subspace] is now a scheme: the open subspaces $H\cap D$, for affine opens $D\subset W$, cover $H$, and Step 6 identifies their induced ringed spaces with affine schemes. This is precisely the local-affineness definition of scheme [def-pc-scheme], using the same sheaf on every overlap. The canonical arrow $j:F\to Z$ has identity maps on local rings under the induced-sheaf stalk identifications, hence is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. It is monic: any two maps into this ringed subspace equal after inclusion have equal continuous maps and equal sheaf maps by inverse-image adjunction [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Its image is $H$ and it is quasi-compact, since Step 1 proves $H\cap D$ quasi-compact for every affine open $D\subset Z$, and the topology on $F$ is the subspace topology. This avoids any quasi-compactness assumption on $Z$ or $Y$.

source.place: Theorem 3.3, proof 2° (open-neighbourhood reduction reversed); §1 Proposition 1.2 and Definition 1.4; canonical ringed-space assembly; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For any test scheme $L$, a morphism $a:L\to Y$ lifts uniquely to $F'$ exactly when $a(|L|)\subset q^{-1}H$, by [lem-sfb-qc-flat-monomorphism-ringed-image]. This is equivalent to $(q\circ a)(|L|)\subset H$, and hence to a unique lift of $q\circ a$ to $F$, by the same node applied to $j$. In particular $qj'$ lifts to a morphism $p:F'\to F$. The equivalence for arbitrary $L$ gives exactly the universal property of $Y\times_ZF$ [def-pc-fibre-product], so the induced map $F'\to Y\times_ZF$ is an isomorphism over $Y$ and the square is cartesian. Neither this identification nor the preceding argument uses flatness of $q$, finite fibres, or Noetherianity of $Y$.

source.place: §1 Proposition 1.2 and Corollary 1.3, applied after Theorem 3.3(ii); primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.
